gloss: to hurt; to injure; to damage

definitions.gloss: to hurt; to injure (a body part)
definitions.explanation: To cause physical injury or pain to a part of the body, especially through strain or overuse.

definitions.gloss: to trouble; to worry; to agonize over
definitions.explanation: To cause mental or emotional distress. Used in the set expression 頭を痛める (to worry over something) and 心を痛める (to be pained by something).

examples.japanese: {走|はし}りすぎて{膝|ひざ}を{痛|いた}めてしまった。
examples.english: I injured my knee from running too much.

examples.japanese: {無理|むり}な{姿勢|しせい}で{仕事|しごと}を{続|つづ}けたせいで、{肩|かた}を{痛|いた}めてしまった。
examples.english: I ended up hurting my shoulder from continuing to work in an awkward position.

examples.japanese: {頭|あたま}を{痛|いた}める{問題|もんだい}だ。
examples.english: It's a problem that gives me a headache.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}の{将来|しょうらい}のことで{頭|あたま}を{痛|いた}めている。
examples.english: I'm worrying over my child's future.

examples.japanese: {被災者|ひさいしゃ}のニュースを{見|み}て{心|こころ}を{痛|いた}めた{人|ひと}は{多|おお}いだろう。
examples.english: Many people must have been saddened by the news about the disaster victims.

notes:
USAGE:
An ichidan ({一段|いちだん}) transitive verb. Takes を to mark the body part or abstract thing being hurt.

KANJI DISTINCTION:
- {痛|いた}める: to hurt, to injure (physical pain or emotional distress)
- {傷|いた}める: to damage, to wound, to spoil (physical damage to objects or food)
- {炒|いた}める: to stir-fry (cooking)
All three are pronounced いためる but have different meanings and kanji.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {腰|こし}を{痛|いた}める: to hurt one's back
- {膝|ひざ}を{痛|いた}める: to injure one's knee
- {頭|あたま}を{痛|いた}める: to worry, to agonize
- {心|こころ}を{痛|いた}める: to be pained, to feel sorrow
- {胃|い}を{痛|いた}める: to upset one's stomach (from stress)
